# Everything docling needs except torch/torchvision (those are in requirements-torch-cpu.txt),
# locked with hashes for linux x86_64, CPython 3.12 (the image's python:3.12-slim-bookworm).
#
# Installed with `pip install --no-deps --require-hashes -r requirements.txt`: every package is
# listed, so pip must not resolve anything on its own, and a changed file fails the build.
#
# Verified against the live cowork-docling:f6885a55 `pip freeze` on 2026-10-06: every package
# matches. Resolved as of 2026-09-21 (after the first working build, 2026-09-20) with docling-slim
# 2.129.0, the version the Dockerfile has always pinned; four packages (filelock, fsspec, numpy,
# setuptools) are held to the live versions by constraints in requirements.in. The CUDA wheels
# PyPI's torch would pull (nvidia-*, cuda-*, triton) are deliberately not emitted.
#
# Regenerate (uv; edit requirements.in first, bump --exclude-newer to the date you resolve on):
#   uv pip compile requirements.in --python-version 3.12 --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 \
#     --generate-hashes --exclude-newer <ISO-DATE> --no-header --no-annotate \
#     --no-emit-package torch --no-emit-package torchvision --no-emit-package triton \
#     --no-emit-package cuda-bindings --no-emit-package cuda-pathfinder --no-emit-package cuda-toolkit \
#     $(for p in cublas cuda-cupti cuda-nvrtc cuda-runtime cudnn-cu13 cufft cufile curand cusolver \
#         cusparse cusparselt-cu13 nccl-cu13 nvjitlink nvshmem-cu13 nvtx; do \
#         echo --no-emit-package nvidia-$p; done) -o requirements.txt
# (then re-add this header). The CUDA package names change with the torch release; if the output
# lists any nvidia-*/cuda-*/triton line, add it to the --no-emit-package list.
